specify DLLs that are loaded at runtime. Programs that improperly or vaguely specify a required DLL may be open to a vulnerability in which an unintended DLL is loaded. Side-loading vulnerabilities specifically occur when Windows Side-by-Side (WinSxS) manifests [1] are not explicit enough about characteristics of the DLL to be loaded. Adversaries may take advantage of a legitimate program that is vulnerable to side-loading to load a malicious DLL. [2] Adversaries likely use this technique as a means of masking actions they perform under a legitimate, trusted system or software process. ID:\xc2 T1073 Tactic: Defense Evasion Platform:\xc2 Windows Data Sources:\xc2 Process use of network, Process monitoring, Loaded DLLs Defense Bypassed:\xc2 Process whitelisting, Anti-virus Version:\xc2 1.0 Mitigations Mitigation Description Audit Use the program sxstrace.exe that is included with Windows along with manual inspection to check manifest files for side-loading vulnerabilities in software. Restrict File and Directory Permissions Install software in write-protected locations. Update Software Update software regularly to include patches that fix DLL side-loading vulnerabilities. Examples Name Description APT19 APT19 launched an HTTP malware variant and a Port 22 malware variant using a legitimate executable that loaded the malicious DLL. [24] APT3 APT3 has been known to side load DLLs with a valid version of Chrome with one of their tools. [26] [10] APT32 APT32 ran legitimately-signed executables from Symantec and McAfee which load a malicious DLL. The group also side-loads its backdoor by dropping a library and a legitimate, signed executable (AcroTranscoder). [19] [27] [28] BADNEWS BADNEWS typically loads its DLL file into a legitimate signed Java or VMware executable. [3] [4] BBSRAT DLL side-loading has been used to execute BBSRAT through a legitimate Citrix executable, ssonsvr.exe. The Citrix executable was dropped along with BBSRAT by the dropper. [9] Denis Denis exploits a security vulnerability to load a fake DLL and execute its code. [19] FinFisher FinFisher uses DLL side-loading to load malicious programs. [6] [7] gh0st RAT A gh0st RAT variant has used DLL side-loading. [5] HTTPBrowser HTTPBrowser has used DLL side-loading. [11] HyperBro HyperBro has used a legitimate application to sideload a DLL to decrypt, decompress, and run a payload. [20] menuPass menuPass has used DLL side-loading to launch versions of Mimikatz and PwDump6 as well as UPPERCUT. [12] [25] OwaAuth OwaAuth has been loaded onto Exchange servers and disguised as an ISAPI filter (DLL file). The IIS w3wp.exe process then loads the malicious DLL. [11] Patchwork A Patchwork .dll that contains BADNEWS is loaded and executed using DLL side-loading. [21] PlugX PlugX has used DLL side-loading to evade anti-virus. [10] [11] [2] [12] [13] Sakula Sakula uses DLL side-loading, typically using a digitally signed sample of Kaspersky Anti-Virus (AV) 6.0 for Windows Workstations or McAfee's Outlook Scan About Box to load malicious DLL files. [8] Soft Cell Soft Cell used DLL side-loading to covertly load PoisonIvy into memory on the victim machine. [30] T9000 During the T9000 installation process, it drops a copy of the legitimate Microsoft binary igfxtray.exe. The executable contains a side-loading weakness which is used to load a portion of the malware. [16] Threat Group-3390 Threat Group-3390 has used DLL side-loading, including by using legitimate Kaspersky antivirus variants in which the DLL acts as a stub loader that loads and executes the shell code. [11] [22] [23] [20] Tropic Trooper Tropic Trooper has been known to side-load DLLs using a valid version of Windows Address Book executable with one of their tools. [29] Wingbird Wingbird side loads a malicious file, sspisrv.dll, in part of a spoofed lssas.exe service. [14] [15] ZeroT ZeroT has used DLL side-loading to load malicious payloads. [17] [18] Detection Monitor processes for unusual activity (e.g., a process that does not use the network begins to do so). Track DLL metadata, such as a hash, and compare DLLs that are loaded at process execution time against previous executions to detect differences that do not correlate with patching or updates.
